title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.

Experimental Setup
We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and
use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics. All the methods
operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling ag-
gregation. We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest

Results
Table 1 presents the performance comparison at both token and
document-levels, the proposed TokenCore ranks first in average
AUROC at both level. At the token-level, ECOD and iForest achieve
the top two positions on SMS_Spam, while TokenCore ranks first
on both Review and Grammar datasets. Deep learning methods
(DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder) consistently rank in the bottom half
across all three datasets. The performance variance across datasets
is substantial, with Review dataset showing AUROC values above
0.80 for top-performing methods, while Grammar remains below
0.65 for all methods. At the document-level, performance metrics
show notable improvements compared to token-level, particularly

for AUPRC. On the Review dataset, both LUNAR and TokenCore
exceed 0.95 AUROC, while maintaining AUPRC above 0.74. The rel-
ative ranking of methods shifts between token and document-levels,
for instance, LOF ranks first on SMS_Spam at document-level but
performs poorly at token-level. The performance patterns across
datasets reflect the characteristics of pre-trained language mod-

import json, re
import numpy as np

nb = json.load(open('repo/demo.ipynb', encoding='utf-8'))

def sentence_lines(cell_idx):
    txt = []
    for o in nb['cells'][cell_idx].get('outputs', []):
        if o.get('output_type') == 'stream':
            txt.append(''.join(o.get('text', [])))
    raw = '\n'.join(txt)
    # lines like: "Sentence 12/550: Great place for great food . I ' ll be back"
    pat = re.compile(r'^Sentence (\d+)/(\d+): (.*)$', re.M)
    out = []
    for m in pat.finditer(raw):
        out.append((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)))
    return out

train_lines = sentence_lines(2)
test_lines = sentence_lines(3)
print('parsed train lines:', len(train_lines), 'test lines:', len(test_lines))

d = np.load('repo/data/restaurant_review.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()
T = [' '.join(t).strip() for t in d['tokens']]
labs = d['labels']
doc_anom = [1 if any(l != 0 for l in ls) else 0 for ls in labs]

index_of = {}
for i, s in enumerate(T):
    index_of.setdefault(s, []).append(i)

def resolve(lines):
    got, miss = {}, 0
    for n, tot, s in lines:
        s2 = s.strip()
        idx = index_of.get(s2)
        if idx is None:
            # fallback: normalized whitespace
            cand = [i for i, t in enumerate(T) if ' '.join(t.split()) == ' '.join(s2.split())]
            idx = cand if cand else None
        if idx is None:
            miss += 1
        else:
            got[n] = idx if len(idx) == 1 else idx
    return got, miss

gtr, mtr = resolve(train_lines)
gte, mte = resolve(test_lines)
print('train matched:', len(gtr), 'missing:', mtr)
print('test  matched:', len(gte), 'missing:', mte)

tr_idx = sorted(v for v in gtr.values() if isinstance(v, int))
te_idx = sorted(v for v in gte.values() if isinstance(v, int))
print('train n:', len(tr_idx), 'anom in train:', sum(doc_anom[i] for i in tr_idx))
print('test  n:', len(te_idx), 'anom in test:', sum(doc_anom[i] for i in te_idx))
print('train idx min/max:', tr_idx[:5], tr_idx[-5:])
print('test idx min/max:', te_idx[:5], te_idx[-5:])
print('overlap train/test:', len(set(tr_idx) & set(te_idx)))
print('union covers:', len(set(tr_idx) | set(te_idx)), 'of', len(T))
np.save('state/recovered_train_idx.npy', np.array(tr_idx))
np.save('state/recovered_test_idx.npy', np.array(te_idx))

T = [' '.join(t).strip() for t in d['tokens']]
doc_anom = np.array([1 if any(l != 0 for l in ls) else 0 for ls in d['labels']])
n = len(T)
normal_idx = np.where(doc_anom == 0)[0]

# unambiguous docs = unique text
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter(T)
uniq = np.array([cnt[t] == 1 for t in T])

tr = set(np.load('state/recovered_train_idx.npy').tolist())
te = set(np.load('state/recovered_test_idx.npy').tolist())
K_tr = {i for i in tr if uniq[i]}
K_te = {i for i in te if uniq[i]}
print('unambiguous known-train:', len(K_tr), 'known-test:', len(K_te))
print('duplicated-text docs in corpus:', sum(1 for u in uniq if not u))

N_TRAIN = n // 2  # 550

def check(train_set):
    return train_set >= K_tr and not (train_set & K_te) and len(train_set) == N_TRAIN

hits = []
MAXS = 30000
for s in range(MAXS):
    # V1/V2/V5: numpy RandomState permutation of normal indices
    rs = np.random.RandomState(s)
    p = rs.permutation(normal_idx)
    if check(set(p[:N_TRAIN].tolist())):
        hits.append(('RandomState-perm-normal', s))
    # V3: default_rng
    p = np.random.default_rng(s).permutation(normal_idx)
    if check(set(p[:N_TRAIN].tolist())):
        hits.append(('default_rng-perm-normal', s))
    # V4: python random shuffle of normal indices
    idx = list(normal_idx)
    random.seed(s)

    if check(set(idx[:N_TRAIN])):
        hits.append(('pyrandom-shuffle-normal', s))
    # V8: permutation of all docs, first N_TRAIN normal ones
    p = np.random.RandomState(s).permutation(n)
    cand = [i for i in p if doc_anom[i] == 0][:N_TRAIN]
    if check(set(cand)):

    d = np.load(f'repo/data/{name}.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()

    for mn in ['bert-base-uncased', 'bert-base-cased']:
        tk = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(mn)
        enc = tk(toks, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True)
        nsub = [len(x) for x in enc['input_ids']]
        dropped = 0
        overflow_docs = 0
        for i, ids in enumerate(enc['input_ids']):
            wids = set(enc.word_ids(i))
            n_words = len([w for w in wids if w is not None])
            if n_words < len(toks[i]):
                dropped += len(toks[i]) - n_words
                overflow_docs += 1
        print(f"   {mn}: max_subwords={max(nsub)} docs_with_dropped_words={overflow_docs} words_dropped={dropped}")

"""Data loading + the authors' train/test split procedure.

Split procedure (reconstructed, and validated against the authors' frozen
Demo.ipynb outputs on restaurant_review -- see reproduce.py --validation):
    n_train = len(all_documents) // 2
    perm    = np.random.RandomState(seed).permutation(normal_doc_indices)
    train   = perm[:n_train]                      # normal documents only
    test    = perm[n_train:] + all_anomalous_docs # rest of normal + all anomalies

Evidence:
  * Demo.ipynb extracts embeddings for 550 train and 550 test documents of the
    1,100-document restaurant_review benchmark.
  * The split recovered from the demo's frozen stdout has 0 anomalous documents
    in train and all 50 anomalous documents in test.
  * np.random.RandomState(42).permutation(normal_idx)[:550] reproduces the
    recovered split exactly on all 1,082 uniquely-identified documents.
The paper states: "We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of
data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly." (Sec. 6.1)
"""
import os
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA_FILES = {
    'grammar': os.path.join(ROOT, 'repo', 'data', 'grammar.npy'),
    'restaurant_review': os.path.join(ROOT, 'repo', 'data', 'restaurant_review.npy'),
    'sms_spam': os.path.join(ROOT, 'repo', 'data', 'sms_spam.npy'),
}
# (n_documents, n_normal, n_anomalous) per the paper's Sec. 4 / repo README
EXPECTED_COUNTS = {
    'grammar': (300, 270, 30),
    'restaurant_review': (1100, 1050, 50),
    'sms_spam': (4518, 4125, 393),
}
DEFAULT_SEED = 42


def load_dataset(name):
    """Return (words, token_labels, doc_anom) with strict consistency checks."""
    path = DATA_FILES[name]
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    words = [list(t) for t in data['tokens']]
    labels = [[int(l) for l in ls] for ls in data['labels']]
    assert len(words) == len(labels), 'tokens/labels length mismatch'
    for i, (w, l) in enumerate(zip(words, labels)):
        assert len(w) == len(l), f'doc {i}: {len(w)} words vs {len(l)} labels'
    doc_anom = np.array([1 if any(l != 0 for l in ls) else 0 for ls in labels], dtype=int)
    n_docs, n_anom = len(words), int(doc_anom.sum())
    exp = EXPECTED_COUNTS[name]
    assert (n_docs, n_docs - n_anom, n_anom) == exp, \
        f'{name}: got {(n_docs, n_docs - n_anom, n_anom)} expected {exp}'
    # R11: a document is anomalous iff it contains at least one anomalous token
    for i, ls in enumerate(labels):
        assert doc_anom[i] == int(any(l != 0 for l in ls)), f'doc {i} label inconsistent'
    return words, labels, doc_anom


def split_authors(doc_anom, seed=DEFAULT_SEED):
    """The authors' split: 50% of ALL documents, drawn from the normal pool, as
    training; the remaining normal documents plus every anomalous document as
    test. Returns (train_idx, test_idx)."""
    doc_anom = np.asarray(doc_anom)
    normal_idx = np.where(doc_anom == 0)[0]
    anom_idx = np.where(doc_anom == 1)[0]
    n_train = len(doc_anom) // 2
    assert n_train <= len(normal_idx), 'more train docs requested than normal docs'
    perm = np.random.RandomState(seed).permutation(normal_idx)
    train_idx = perm[:n_train]
    test_idx = np.concatenate([perm[n_train:], anom_idx]).astype(int)
    return train_idx.astype(int), test_idx


def split_authors_forced(doc_anom, n_normal_train, n_anom_test, seed=DEFAULT_SEED):
    """Smoke-test variant: keep only the first n_normal_train normal and the
    first n_anom_test anomalous documents, then apply the same procedure."""
    keep_normal = np.where(doc_anom == 0)[0][:n_normal_train]
    keep_anom = np.where(doc_anom == 1)[0][:n_anom_test]
    sub = np.concatenate([keep_normal, keep_anom])
    sub_anom = doc_anom[sub]
    train_local, test_local = split_authors(sub_anom, seed=seed)
    return sub[train_local], sub[test_local]


def dataset_stats(words, labels, doc_anom, train_idx, test_idx):
    n_tok_all = sum(len(w) for w in words)
    n_pos_all = sum(1 for ls in labels for l in ls if l != 0)
    train_tok = sum(len(words[i]) for i in train_idx)
    train_pos = sum(1 for i in train_idx for l in labels[i] if l != 0)
    test_tok = sum(len(words[i]) for i in test_idx)
    test_pos = sum(1 for i in test_idx for l in labels[i] if l != 0)
    return {
        'n_docs': len(words),
        'n_train_docs': int(len(train_idx)),
        'n_test_docs': int(len(test_idx)),
        'n_anomalous_docs': int(doc_anom.sum()),
        'n_tokens_total': n_tok_all,
        'n_positive_tokens_total': n_pos_all,
        'n_train_tokens': train_tok,
        'n_train_positive_tokens': train_pos,
        'n_test_tokens': test_tok,
        'n_test_positive_tokens': test_pos,
        'test_positive_rate': float(test_pos / test_tok) if test_tok else 0.0,
    }

"""BERT word-level embedding extraction (max pooling over subwords, Eq. 1).

This mirrors the authors' align.py::extract_word_embeddings, but vectorised and
quiet: for every document we tokenize the gold word list with
`is_split_into_words=True`, run BERT-base, drop the [CLS]/[SEP] special-token
positions, and aggregate each word's subword vectors with an element-wise max
(Eq. 1 of the paper):

    e_token = max(e_1, ..., e_n)     (element-wise over embedding dimensions)

No truncation happens for these benchmarks (checked: max 420 subwords < 512),
so every gold word receives exactly one word unit (alignment coverage 1.0).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch


def resolve_model_path(model_name):
    """Use a local snapshot under REPRO_DATA_CACHE when available (offline-safe)."""
    cache = os.environ.get('REPRO_DATA_CACHE')
    if cache:
        local = os.path.join(cache, 'models', model_name)
        if os.path.isdir(local) and os.path.exists(os.path.join(local, 'config.json')):
            return local
    return model_name


import os


def extract_word_embeddings(model, tokenizer, all_tokens, all_labels, device='cpu',
                            verbose_every=500, tag=''):
    """Per-document BERT forward pass -> word-level (max-pooled) embeddings.

    Returns
    -------
    X : (n_word_units_total, hidden) float32 -- flattened over all documents
    y : (n_word_units_total,) int -- token-level gold labels
    doc_spans : list[list[int]] -- per document, the row indices in X
    coverage : float -- fraction of gold words that received a word unit
    """
    n_words_total = sum(len(w) for w in all_tokens)
    rows, ys, doc_spans = [], [], []
    n_units = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i, words in enumerate(all_tokens):
            enc = tokenizer(words, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                            return_tensors='pt')
            input_ids = enc['input_ids'].to(device)
            attention_mask = enc['attention_mask'].to(device)
            hs = model(input_ids=input_ids,
                       attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state[0]
            hs = hs.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(0)
            # group subword positions by gold word index
            by_word = {}
            for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                if w is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                by_word.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
            span = []
            for w in sorted(by_word):
                positions = by_word[w]
                if len(positions) == 1:
                    emb = hs[positions[0]]
                else:
                    emb = hs[positions].max(axis=0)  # element-wise max, Eq. 1
                rows.append(emb)
                ys.append(int(all_labels[i][w]))
                span.append(n_units)
                n_units += 1
            doc_spans.append(span)
            if verbose_every and (i + 1) % verbose_every == 0:
                print(f'  [{tag}] embedded {i + 1}/{len(all_tokens)} docs', flush=True)
    X = np.stack(rows) if rows else np.zeros((0, model.config.hidden_size), np.float32)
    y = np.array(ys, dtype=int)
    coverage = n_units / n_words_total if n_words_total else 1.0
    return X, y, doc_spans, coverage


def max_pool_is_elementwise(hs, positions):
    """Hand-check helper: element-wise max over the subword vectors."""
    return np.max(hs[positions], axis=0)

"""Metrics: token-level AUROC/AUPRC (pooled over all test tokens), document-level
AUROC/AUPRC via mean aggregation of token scores (Eq. 3), plus sanity controls."""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score


def token_metrics(y_true, scores):
    return {
        'auroc': float(roc_auc_score(y_true, scores)),
        'auprc': float(average_precision_score(y_true, scores)),
        'n_tokens': int(len(y_true)),
        'n_positive': int(np.sum(y_true)),
    }


def doc_metrics(doc_labels, doc_scores):
    return {
        'auroc': float(roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
        'auprc': float(average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
        'n_docs': int(len(doc_labels)),
        'n_positive': int(np.sum(doc_labels)),
    }


def doc_scores_from_token_scores(doc_spans, token_scores):
    """Eq. (3): s_doc = (1/T) * sum_i s_token_i over the document's tokens."""
    out, labels_idx = [], []
    for span in doc_spans:
        if len(span) == 0:
            continue
        out.append(float(np.mean(token_scores[span])))
        labels_idx.append(span)
    return np.array(out, dtype=float)


def manual_auroc(y_true, scores):
    """Rank-based AUROC implementation used only to cross-check sklearn."""
    y = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
    order = np.argsort(s, kind='mergesort')
    ranks = np.empty(len(s), dtype=float)
    sorted_s = s[order]
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(s) and sorted_s[j + 1] == sorted_s[i]:
            j += 1
        ranks[order[i:j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j) + 1.0  # average rank for ties
        i = j + 1
    n_pos = int(y.sum())
    n_neg = len(y) - n_pos
    if n_pos == 0 or n_neg == 0:
        return float('nan')
    return float((ranks[y == 1].sum() - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (n_pos * n_neg))


def parity_check():
    """Verify the metric plumbing: manual rank AUROC vs sklearn on synthetic data,
    plus a random-score control (AUROC ~ 0.5, AUPRC ~ positive rate)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    y = (rng.rand(2000) < 0.05).astype(int)
    y[:10] = 1
    s = rng.rand(2000)
    diff = abs(manual_auroc(y, s) - roc_auc_score(y, s))
    assert diff < 1e-12, f'AUROC parity failed: {diff}'
    # tied scores
    s_tied = np.round(s, 1)
    diff_t = abs(manual_auroc(y, s_tied) - roc_auc_score(y, s_tied))
    assert diff_t < 1e-12, f'AUROC parity with ties failed: {diff_t}'
    # random control on an imbalanced problem
    y2 = (rng.rand(5000) < 0.02).astype(int)
    y2[:20] = 1
    s2 = rng.rand(5000)
    a, p = roc_auc_score(y2, s2), average_precision_score(y2, s2)
    assert 0.45 < a < 0.55, f'random AUROC control failed: {a}'
    assert abs(p - y2.mean()) < 0.02, f'random AUPRC control failed: {p}'
    return {'sklearn_vs_manual_max_abs_diff': float(diff), 'random_auroc': float(a),
            'random_auprc': float(p), 'random_positive_rate': float(y2.mean())}

"""Download the BERT backbone(s) once into $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/models/<name> so that
reproduce.py can run offline. Called automatically by reproduce.py when the local
snapshot is missing."""
import os
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, 'src'))


def ensure_model(model_name):
    cache = os.environ.get('REPRO_DATA_CACHE')
    local = os.path.join(cache, 'models', model_name) if cache else None
    if local and os.path.exists(os.path.join(local, 'config.json')):
        return local
    from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
    kwargs = dict(allow_patterns=[
        'config.json', 'vocab.txt', 'tokenizer.json', 'tokenizer_config.json',
        'model.safetensors', 'pytorch_model.bin',
    ])
    path = snapshot_download(model_name, **kwargs)
    if local:
        os.makedirs(local, exist_ok=True)
        # link/copy the few needed files into the shared cache
        import shutil
        for f in os.listdir(path):
            src = os.path.join(path, f)
            dst = os.path.join(local, f)
            if not os.path.exists(dst):
                shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        return local
    return path


if __name__ == '__main__':
    for name in sys.argv[1:] or ['bert-base-uncased', 'bert-base-cased']:
        p = ensure_model(name)
        print(name, '->', p)

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduction driver for "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection" (WWW '26).

Primary target (claim C1): TokenCore TOKEN-LEVEL AUROC on the Grammar benchmark
(Table 1, Token section, TokenCore x Grammar ROC), produced with:
  * bert-base-uncased last-hidden-state embeddings,
  * element-wise MAX pooling of subwords into word units (Eq. 1),
  * a memory bank of every word embedding of the normal TRAINING documents,
  * token score = L2 distance to the nearest bank entry (Eq. 2),
  * document score = mean of its token scores (Eq. 3),
  * the authors' split: 50% of all documents, drawn from the normal pool, as
    training; the rest (normal + all anomalous) as test (seed 42, recovered and
    validated against the authors' frozen Demo.ipynb outputs).

Also reported (same pipeline): Grammar token AUPRC (C2), Review / SMS_Spam token
AUROC (C3/C4), the three-dataset token averages (C5/C6) and document-level
AUROC incl. Review (C7/C8).

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                  # full run, writes results/metrics.json
  python reproduce.py --smoke          # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
  python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 42
"""
import argparse

import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

    # demo pipeline on restaurant_review with bert-base-cased. Used only as a
    # pipeline-correctness cross-check of our re-implementation.
    'dataset': 'restaurant_review',
    'model': 'bert-base-cased',
    'token_auroc': 0.8291871975956033,
    'provenance': "authors' demo.ipynb frozen output (repo, not the paper)",
    'tolerance': 0.01,
}
PRIMARY_SEED = tad_data.DEFAULT_SEED  # 42
SPREAD_SEEDS = [42, 0, 1, 2]


def log(msg):
    print(msg, flush=True)


def get_embeddings(dataset, model_key, tokenizer, model, device, cache_dir):
    """Embed every document once per (dataset, backbone); cache on disk."""
    words, labels, doc_anom = tad_data.load_dataset(dataset)
    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    import hashlib
    h = hashlib.md5(open(tad_data.DATA_FILES[dataset], 'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:10]
    key = os.path.join(cache_dir, f'emb_{model_key}_{dataset}_{h}.npz')
    if os.path.exists(key):
        z = np.load(key)
        if z['X'].shape[0] == z['y'].shape[0] and z['doc_ids'].shape[0] == z['y'].shape[0]:
            log(f'  [cache] loaded embeddings {key} X={z["X"].shape}')
            return words, labels, doc_anom, z['X'], z['y'], z['doc_ids']
    t0 = time.time()
    X, y, doc_spans, coverage = tad_embed.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tokenizer, words, labels, device=device, verbose_every=500,
        tag=f'{dataset}/{model_key}')
    doc_ids = np.concatenate([np.full(len(s), i, dtype=np.int32)
                              for i, s in enumerate(doc_spans)])
    log(f'  embedded {len(words)} docs -> {X.shape} word units '
        f'(coverage {coverage:.4f}) in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s')
    assert coverage == 1.0, f'alignment coverage {coverage} != 1.0'
    np.savez_compressed(key, X=X, y=y, doc_ids=doc_ids)
    return words, labels, doc_anom, X, y, doc_ids


def evaluate_split(X, y, doc_anom, rows_per_doc, train_idx, test_idx):
    """One split -> memory bank -> token scores -> token/doc metrics."""

    assert len(X_bank) > 0 and y_bank.sum() == 0, \

    det.fit(X_bank)
    scores = det.decision_function(X[test_rows])
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(scores))
    tok = tad_eval.token_metrics(y[test_rows], scores)
    doc_labels = doc_anom[test_idx]

"""BERT word-level embedding extraction (max pooling over subwords, Eq. 1).

This mirrors the authors' align.py::extract_word_embeddings, but vectorised and
quiet: for every document we tokenize the gold word list with
`is_split_into_words=True`, run BERT-base, drop the [CLS]/[SEP] special-token
positions, and aggregate each word's subword vectors with an element-wise max
(Eq. 1 of the paper):

    e_token = max(e_1, ..., e_n)     (element-wise over embedding dimensions)

No truncation happens for these benchmarks (checked: max 420 subwords < 512),
so every gold word receives exactly one word unit (alignment coverage 1.0).

Spans are the single source of truth for document boundaries: the extractor
returns, for every document, its exact (start, end) span into the global word
matrix X, and every downstream consumer must use those spans (never offsets
recomputed from gold token counts).
"""
import os

import numpy as np
import torch


def resolve_model_path(model_name):
    """Use a local snapshot under REPRO_DATA_CACHE when available (offline-safe)."""
    cache = os.environ.get('REPRO_DATA_CACHE')
    if cache:
        local = os.path.join(cache, 'models', model_name)
        if os.path.isdir(local) and os.path.exists(os.path.join(local, 'config.json')):
            return local
    return model_name


def pool_subwords(hs, positions):
    """Eq. (1): element-wise max over the subword vectors of one word."""
    if len(positions) == 1:
        return hs[positions[0]]
    return hs[positions].max(axis=0)


def _diagnose(doc_i, doc_spans, all_tokens, tokenizer, n_units, cursor, s, e):
    """Print everything needed to see which word lost/gained a unit."""
    print(f'--- span assertion failed at document {doc_i} ---', flush=True)
    print(f'X holds {n_units} word units; expected cursor before doc {doc_i} = '
          f'{cursor}; its span = ({s}, {e})')
    if all_tokens is None:
        return
    words = list(all_tokens[doc_i])
    print(f'gold words ({len(words)}): {words}')
    if tokenizer is None:
        return
    enc = tokenizer(words, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True)
    wids = enc.word_ids(0)
    print(f'max_length = {tokenizer.model_max_length}; n_subwords = '
          f'{len(enc["input_ids"])} (incl. [CLS]/[SEP])')
    print(f'tokenizer word_ids = {list(wids)}')
    from collections import Counter
    got = Counter(w for w in wids if w is not None)
    zero = [w for w in range(len(words)) if got.get(w, 0) == 0]
    multi = {w: c for w, c in got.items() if c > 1}
    print(f'words with ZERO subwords (their unit is dropped): {zero}')
    print(f'words split into >1 subwords (max-pooled): {multi}')


def assert_valid_spans(doc_spans, X, all_tokens=None, tokenizer=None):
    """Hard assertion: every span satisfies start <= end <= len(X) and the spans
    partition range(len(X)) in document order. Raises AssertionError with a
    diagnostic dump on failure. Returns True on success."""
    n = len(X)
    cursor = 0
    for i, span in enumerate(doc_spans):
        s, e = int(span[0]), int(span[1])
        if not (0 <= s <= e <= n) or s != cursor:
            _diagnose(i, doc_spans, all_tokens, tokenizer, n, cursor, s, e)
            raise AssertionError(
                f'document {i}: span ({s}, {e}) breaks the partition of '
                f'range({n}) at cursor {cursor}')
        cursor = e
    if cursor != n:
        raise AssertionError(
            f'spans cover {cursor} of {n} word units; they do not partition '
            f'range({n}) (last document index {len(doc_spans) - 1})')
    return True


def extract_word_embeddings(model, tokenizer, all_tokens, all_labels, device='cpu',
                            verbose_every=500, tag=''):
    """Per-document BERT forward pass -> word-level (max-pooled) embeddings.

    Returns
    -------
    X : (n_word_units_total, hidden) float32 -- flattened over all documents
    y : (n_word_units_total,) int -- token-level gold labels
    doc_spans : list[(start, end)] -- per document, its exact span into X/y
    coverage : float -- fraction of gold words that received a word unit
    """
    n_words_total = sum(len(w) for w in all_tokens)
    rows, ys, doc_spans = [], [], []
    n_units = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i, words in enumerate(all_tokens):
            enc = tokenizer(words, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                            return_tensors='pt')
            input_ids = enc['input_ids'].to(device)
            attention_mask = enc['attention_mask'].to(device)
            hs = model(input_ids=input_ids,
                       attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state[0]
            hs = hs.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(0)
            # group subword positions by gold word index
            by_word = {}
            for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                if w is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                by_word.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
            start = n_units
            for w in sorted(by_word):
                emb = pool_subwords(hs, by_word[w])  # element-wise max, Eq. 1
                rows.append(emb)
                ys.append(int(all_labels[i][w]))
                n_units += 1
            doc_spans.append((start, n_units))
            if verbose_every and (i + 1) % verbose_every == 0:
                print(f'  [{tag}] embedded {i + 1}/{len(all_tokens)} docs', flush=True)
    X = np.stack(rows) if rows else np.zeros((0, model.config.hidden_size), np.float32)
    y = np.array(ys, dtype=int)
    assert_valid_spans(doc_spans, X, all_tokens, tokenizer)
    coverage = n_units / n_words_total if n_words_total else 1.0
    return X, y, doc_spans, coverage


def max_pool_is_elementwise(hs, positions):
    """Hand-check helper: element-wise max over the subword vectors."""
    return np.max(hs[positions], axis=0)

def doc_scores_from_token_scores(doc_spans, token_scores):
    """Eq. (3): s_doc = (1/T) * sum_i s_token_i over the document's tokens.

    doc_spans: per-document (start, end) spans into the flat token_scores array
    (the single source of truth produced by the embedding extractor)."""
    n = len(token_scores)
    out = []
    for k, span in enumerate(doc_spans):
        s, e = int(span[0]), int(span[1])
        if not (0 <= s <= e <= n):
            raise AssertionError(
                f'document {k}: span ({s}, {e}) out of bounds for token_scores '
                f'of length {n}')
        out.append(float(np.mean(token_scores[s:e])))
    return np.array(out, dtype=float)

def get_embeddings(dataset, words, labels, doc_anom, model_key, tokenizer, model,
                   device, cache_dir, smoke=False):
    """Embed every document once per (dataset, backbone, doc subset); cache on disk.

    Returns (X, y, doc_spans) with doc_spans the per-document (start, end) spans
    into X produced by the embedding extractor (single source of truth)."""
    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    import hashlib
    h = hashlib.md5(open(tad_data.DATA_FILES[dataset], 'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:10]
    key = os.path.join(cache_dir, f'emb_{model_key}_{dataset}_{h}_{len(words)}.npz')
    if os.path.exists(key):
        z = np.load(key)
        spans = [tuple(map(int, s)) for s in z['spans']]
        if (z['X'].shape[0] == z['y'].shape[0] == int(z['spans'][-1][-1])
                and len(spans) == len(words) and z['X'].shape[1] == 768
                and tad_embed.assert_valid_spans(spans, z['X'])):
            log(f'  [cache] loaded embeddings {key} X={z["X"].shape}')
            return z['X'], z['y'], spans
        log(f'  [cache] stale/invalid cache {key} -> recomputing')
    t0 = time.time()
    X, y, doc_spans, coverage = tad_embed.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tokenizer, words, labels, device=device, verbose_every=500,
        tag=f'{dataset}/{model_key}{"-smoke" if smoke else ""}')
    log(f'  embedded {len(words)} docs -> {X.shape} word units '
        f'(coverage {coverage:.4f}) in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s')
    assert coverage == 1.0, f'alignment coverage {coverage} != 1.0'
    tad_embed.assert_valid_spans(doc_spans, X, words, tokenizer)
    np.savez_compressed(key, X=X, y=y,
                        spans=np.asarray(doc_spans, dtype=np.int32))
    return X, y, doc_spans


def evaluate_split(X, y, doc_anom, doc_spans, train_idx, test_idx, seed=0):
    """One split -> memory bank -> token scores -> token/doc metrics.

    doc_spans must partition range(len(X)); this is asserted before evaluation.
    """

def get_embeddings(dataset, model_key, tokenizer, model, device, cache_dir):
    """Embed every document once per (dataset, backbone); cache on disk."""
    words, labels, doc_anom = tad_data.load_dataset(dataset)
    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    import hashlib
    h = hashlib.md5(open(tad_data.DATA_FILES[dataset], 'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:10]
    key = os.path.join(cache_dir, f'emb_{model_key}_{dataset}_{h}_{len(words)}.npz')
    if os.path.exists(key):
        z = np.load(key)
        if (z['X'].shape[0] == z['y'].shape[0] == z['doc_ids'].shape[0]
                and int(z['doc_ids'].max()) == len(words) - 1
                and z['X'].shape[1] == 768):
            log(f'  [cache] loaded embeddings {key} X={z["X"].shape}')
            return words, labels, doc_anom, z['X'], z['y'], z['doc_ids']
        log(f'  [cache] stale/invalid cache {key} -> recomputing')
    t0 = time.time()
    X, y, doc_spans, coverage = tad_embed.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tokenizer, words, labels, device=device, verbose_every=500,
        tag=f'{dataset}/{model_key}')
    doc_ids = np.concatenate([np.full(len(s), i, dtype=np.int32)
                              for i, s in enumerate(doc_spans)])
    log(f'  embedded {len(words)} docs -> {X.shape} word units '
        f'(coverage {coverage:.4f}) in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s')
    assert coverage == 1.0, f'alignment coverage {coverage} != 1.0'
    np.savez_compressed(key, X=X, y=y, doc_ids=doc_ids)
    return words, labels, doc_anom, X, y, doc_ids


def evaluate_split(X, y, doc_anom, rows_per_doc, train_idx, test_idx):

    test_rows = np.concatenate([rows_per_doc[i] for i in test_idx])

"""Verify the batched forward pass reproduces the per-document forward pass."""
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'src'))
import numpy as np
import torch
import tad_data, tad_embed
from tad_embed import pool_subwords
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

torch.set_num_threads(7)
path = tad_embed.resolve_model_path('bert-base-uncased')
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path)
mdl = AutoModel.from_pretrained(path).eval()

words, labels, doc_anom = tad_data.load_dataset('grammar')
# mix normal and anomalous docs
keep = list(range(4)) + [270, 271]
words = [words[i] for i in keep]
labels = [labels[i] for i in keep]

# --- per-doc ---
rows, ys, spans = [], [], []
n = 0
with torch.no_grad():
    for i, ws in enumerate(words):
        enc = tok(ws, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt')
        hs = mdl(input_ids=enc['input_ids'], attention_mask=enc['attention_mask']
                 ).last_hidden_state[0].numpy().astype(np.float32)
        by = {}
        for p, w in enumerate(enc.word_ids(0)):
            if w is not None:
                by.setdefault(w, []).append(p)
        s = n
        for w in sorted(by):
            rows.append(pool_subwords(hs, by[w])); ys.append(labels[i][w]); n += 1
        spans.append((s, n))
X1 = np.stack(rows); y1 = np.array(ys)

# --- batched (as in tad_embed.extract_word_embeddings) ---
X2, y2, spans2, cov = tad_embed.extract_word_embeddings(mdl, tok, words, labels)

print('per-doc X', X1.shape, 'batched X', X2.shape)
print('labels equal:', np.array_equal(y1, y2), 'spans equal:', spans == spans2)
print('max abs diff:', float(np.abs(X1 - X2).max()))
print('mean abs diff:', float(np.abs(X1 - X2).mean()))
assert X1.shape == X2.shape and np.array_equal(y1, y2) and spans == spans2
assert np.abs(X1 - X2).max() < 1e-3, 'batched/per-doc embedding mismatch'
# max-pool hand check on a multi-subword word
multi = None
for j, ws in enumerate(words):
    enc = tok(ws, is_split_into_words=True, return_offsets_mapping=False)
    wids = enc.word_ids(0)
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter(w for w in wids if w is not None)
    for w, cnt in c.items():
        if cnt > 1:
            multi = (j, w, cnt)
            break
    if multi:
        break
j, w, cnt = multi
enc = tok(words[j], is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors='pt')
with torch.no_grad():
    hs = mdl(input_ids=enc['input_ids'], attention_mask=enc['attention_mask']
             ).last_hidden_state[0].numpy().astype(np.float32)
by = {}
for p, wid in enumerate(enc.word_ids(0)):
    if wid is not None:
        by.setdefault(wid, []).append(p)
pos = by[w]
pooled = pool_subwords(hs, pos)
print(f'max-pool hand check: word "{words[j][w]}" has {cnt} subwords; '
      f'pooled == coord-wise max: {np.allclose(pooled, hs[pos].max(0))}; '
      f'pooled != first subword: {not np.allclose(pooled, hs[pos[0]])}; '
      f'pooled != mean: {not np.allclose(pooled, hs[pos].mean(0))}')
assert np.allclose(pooled, hs[pos].max(0))
print('OK: batched == per-doc; max pooling verified')

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The TokenCore pipeline is implemented faithfully and largely with the authors' own artefacts: repo/TokenCore.py is imported verbatim as the nearest-neighbour detector, BERT-base-uncased last-hidden-state word embeddings are formed by element-wise max pooling over subwords (unit- and hand-checked against first-subword/mean), the memory bank contains only normal training tokens (asserted), and the split procedure was recovered from the authors' demo.ipynb and validated against its frozen Review output to |diff|=9.8e-8 with bert-base-cased — strong evidence that the embedding/split/scoring plumbing is the authors' pipeline, not an easier re-implementation. On the match target (Grammar token AUROC) the run gives 0.6137 vs the paper's 0.6371 (|diff|=0.0234, just outside the 0.02 band); across four split seeds the value ranges 0.5633-0.6295 (std 0.0248) on only 47 positive tokens, so the gap is consistent with split randomness plus an unspecified pooling/layer/seed choice (A5/A3/A8). There is no cheating: metrics come from sklearn on the released data, a random-score control yields 0.50, manual and sklearn AUROC agree to 0.0, and the only external number in the code (0.829187) is a repo-artefact demo output used solely as a pipeline cross-check, not a paper table value. The major fidelity gap is scope, not method: the six required baselines (LOF/iForest/ECOD/DeepSVDD/AutoEncoder/LUNAR) were never implemented ('run time budget reached'), so R8 is missing and the paper's ranking claims (C5/C7 'first among 7 methods') are unverifiable. Minor bookkeeping bug: the per-dataset 'stats' block is computed after the seed loop and therefore reflects the last spread seed (2) rather than the primary seed 42, causing small inconsistencies between the reported split text (1419 test tokens) and the stats block (1395).

requirement_check.evidence: src/tad_embed.py runs bert-base-uncased last_hidden_state with element-wise max pooling and that is the only backbone used for the reported numbers (metrics.json config.backbone='bert-base-uncased'), so R1 holds for TokenCore. But the six baseline methods are never run (only TokenCore exists), so the 'all methods operate on the same embeddings' statement is not instantiated for a comparison. Also note the authors' own released demo pipeline (which this code matches to 9.8e-8) uses bert-base-cased, contradicting the paper's 'uncased' text.

tad_embed.pool_subwords returns hs[positions].max(axis=0) for multi-subword words; reproduce.py unit_checks asserts pooled != first subword and pooled != mean on a synthetic 2-subword example, and src/check_equiv.py hand-verifies pooled == hs[pos].max(0) on a real multi-subword word.

evaluate_split builds bank_rows only from train_idx documents and hard-asserts y_bank.sum()==0 ('memory bank must contain normal training tokens only'); reported n_train_positive_tokens=0 for all three datasets.

src/tad_detector.py wraps the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py: TokenCore(n_neighbors=1).fit(X_bank) then decision_function -> NearestNeighbors k=1, minkowski p=2 (Euclidean) minimum distance, matching Eq. (2); higher score = more anomalous.

tad_eval.doc_scores_from_token_scores takes np.mean of each document's token-score span (Eq. 3); doc AUROC/AUPRC are reported separately from token-level metrics for all three datasets (e.g. Grammar doc AUROC 0.5678, Review 0.9308).

tad_data.split_authors: n_train = len(docs)//2 sampled from the normal indices with RandomState(seed=42); remaining normal docs + all anomalous docs form the test set. This was recovered from the authors' demo.ipynb stdout and reproduces the authors' frozen Review token AUROC to |diff|=9.8e-8. Caveat: this is 50% of ALL documents drawn from the normal pool (Grammar 150/300 train = 55.6% of the 270 normal docs), not literally '50% of the normal documents' (which would be 135); it matches the authors' code rather than the paper's wording.

tad_eval.token_metrics/doc_metrics use sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score; metrics.json reports token and document AUROC and AUPRC for Grammar, Review, SMS_Spam and their averages (C2=0.0390, C6=0.0466, C1=0.6137, C5=0.6893, C7=0.6821).

No LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder or LUNAR code exists anywhere in the workspace; only TokenCore is instantiated (src/tad_detector.py). The implementer summary is 'run time budget reached'. Consequently the paper's headline ranking claims (C5/C7 'ranks first among 7 methods') cannot be evaluated at all — only TokenCore's own numbers are produced.

extract_word_embeddings groups subword positions with enc.word_ids() and pools per gold word, asserting coverage==1.0 (2746 word units for 2746 gold Grammar tokens) plus span-partition assertions in assert_valid_spans; src/check_equiv.py confirms batched == per-document extraction (|diff| < 1e-3).

tad_data.EXPECTED_COUNTS hard-asserts (300, 270, 30) for grammar and load_dataset succeeds on the authors' released repo/data/grammar.npy; reported stats n_docs=300, n_anomalous_docs=30, 47 anomalous tokens overall (1.7% token anomaly rate).

tad_data.load_dataset computes doc_anom = any(label != 0) and asserts per-document consistency with the token labels; doc labels used in tad_eval.doc_metrics therefore follow the 'at least one anomalous token' definition.

divergence_causes: randomness: the paper reports no seed for the Grammar split; the reproduced Grammar token AUROC over splits {42,0,1,2} is 0.6137/0.6295/0.5928/0.5633 (mean 0.5998, std 0.0248) on only 47 positive tokens out of 1419, so the paper's 0.6371 sits ~1.5 sigma above the seed mean and a 0.023 gap is within split noise.

paper_underspecified (A5 token-AUROC pooling, A3 hidden layer, A1 distance metric, A8 split seed, A11 sampling of the 270/30 Grammar sentences): the paper never states the pooling scheme for token-level AUROC, the BERT layer, or the split seed, so part of the residual gap is not attributable to the implementation.

paper_underspecified (R1 backbone inconsistency): the code reproduces the authors' released demo.ipynb Review output to 9.8e-8 but only with bert-base-cased, whose token AUROC 0.8292 is within 0.002 of the paper's Review value 0.8271, while the paper's text says bert-base-uncased (which this run follows, giving 0.8794). This suggests the paper's Table 1 numbers may come from a cased backbone, which would systematically shift the Grammar value too.
